title: Mississippi: history overview
d: Mississippi: the Magnolia State, admitted 1817 (20th); capital Jackson.
definition: Mississippi: the Magnolia State, admitted 1817 (20th); capital Jackson.
description: Mississippi — "Magnolia State" — entered the Union 1817 (20th). Its capital is Jackson and its largest city is Jackson. Choctaw and Chickasaw; cotton kingdom. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Mississippi achieved statehood 1817 (20th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Civil War; civil rights struggle. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Mississippi its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Mississippi went from territory to state.
definition: How Mississippi went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Mississippi: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Blues birthplace. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Mississippi's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Jackson
d: Jackson is the capital of Mississippi.
definition: Jackson is the capital of Mississippi.
description: Jackson has been the seat of Mississippi government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Mississippi's largest is Jackson — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Magnolia State
description: The nickname "Magnolia State" captures how Mississippi sees itself — and how America sees it. The blues was born in the Delta. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Virtute et armis (By valor and arms)."

title: Motto: Virtute et armis (By valor and arms)
t: Motto: Virtute et armis (By valor and arms)
d: The state motto of Mississippi is "Virtute et armis (By valor and arms)."
definition: The state motto of Mississippi is "Virtute et armis (By valor and arms)."
description: The motto "Virtute et armis (By valor and arms)" is Mississippi's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Magnolia on blue with gold bars (2020). Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
